request.user:
[2022 summer phd math-stat — problem 2]

Training data $(x_i, y_i)$, $1 \le i \le n$, are i.i.d. as $(x, y)$ with $y = x^T \beta^* + \varepsilon$, $x \in \mathbb{R}^p$, $\varepsilon$ independent of $x$, under (A1) $\varepsilon$ sub-Gaussian with parameter $\sigma$: $P(|\varepsilon| \ge t) \le 2e^{-t^2/(2\sigma^2)}$; (A2) $|x| \le B_0$ a.s. Let $\hat\beta = \arg\min_\beta \{\ell_n(\beta) + \lambda\|\beta\|_1\}$ with $\ell_n(\beta) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_i (y_i - x_i^T\beta)^2$. Let $(x_0, y_0)$ be an independent test point; study the out-of-sample error $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}$ (conditional on training data). Set $\lambda_0 = \sqrt{\log(p/\delta)/n}$. You may use results from preceding questions regardless of whether you answered them.
(i) Show $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} = \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2\}$.
(ii) With $\Sigma = \mathbb{E}(x x^T)$ and $\tilde\Sigma = n^{-1}\sum_i x_i x_i^T$: for sufficiently small $\delta > 0$, show with probability $1 - k_1\delta$ that $\|\tilde\Sigma - \Sigma\|_{\max} \le B_1\lambda_0$ (constant $B_1$ depending on $B_0$). Call this event $\Omega_1$.
(iii) Under (A3) $b^T\Sigma b \ge (\nu_0^*)^2 \sum_j b_j^2$ and (A4) $|S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0 \le \eta_0$: show that on $\Omega_1$, $\nu_0^2(\sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|)^2 \le |S_{\beta^*}|(b^T\tilde\Sigma b)$ for any $b$ with $\sum_{j \notin S_{\beta^*}}|b_j| \le \xi_0 \sum_{j \in S_{\beta^*}}|b_j|$ (a restricted-eigenvalue / compatibility condition on $\tilde\Sigma$).
(iv) Under (A1)-(A4), formulate an event $\Omega_2$ with $P(\Omega_2) \ge 1 - k_2\delta$ such that on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$, for a suitable $\lambda$: $\frac1n\sum_i (x_i^T(\hat\beta - \beta^*))^2 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$ and $\|\hat\beta - \beta^*\|_1 \le M_0 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0$. Prove $P(\Omega_2) \ge 1 - k_2\delta$ for your $\Omega_2$ (you need not prove the two displayed bounds).
(v) For that $\lambda$, show on $\Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2$ that $\mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\} \le \mathbb{E}_{out}\{(y_0 - x_0^T\beta^*)^2\} + M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2$.

Assume, as is standard/necessary here, that \(\mathbb E\varepsilon=0\). Let

\[
S:=S_{\beta^*}=\{j:\beta^*_j\neq 0\},\qquad s:=|S|,\qquad \Delta:=\hat\beta-\beta^*,
\]

and write \(\|A\|_{\max}=\max_{j,k}|A_{jk}|\).

---

## (i)

Since \(y_0=x_0^T\beta^*+\varepsilon_0\),

\[
y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta
=\varepsilon_0-x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)
=\varepsilon_0-x_0^T\Delta .
\]

Conditional on the training data, \(\Delta\) is fixed, and \((x_0,\varepsilon_0)\) is independent of the training data. Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
&=\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(\varepsilon_0-x_0^T\Delta)^2\}\\
&=\mathbb E\varepsilon_0^2+\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T\Delta)^2\}
-2\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{\varepsilon_0 x_0^T\Delta\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Because \(\varepsilon_0\) is independent of \(x_0\), \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_0=0\), and \(\Delta\) is fixed conditionally on the training data,

\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{\varepsilon_0 x_0^T\Delta\}
=(\mathbb E\varepsilon_0)\,\mathbb E(x_0^T\Delta)=0.
\]

Also,

\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
=\mathbb E\varepsilon_0^2.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*))^2\}.
}
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(x_0^T\Delta)^2\}=\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta.
\]

---

## (ii)

For fixed \(j,k\),

\[
\tilde\Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \left(x_{ij}x_{ik}-\mathbb E[x_jx_k]\right).
\]

Since \(|x_i|\le B_0\) a.s., each coordinate satisfies \(|x_{ij}|\le B_0\), hence

\[
|x_{ij}x_{ik}|\le B_0^2.
\]

By Hoeffding’s inequality, for every \(t>0\),

\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|\tilde\Sigma_{jk}-\Sigma_{jk}\right|\ge t\right)
\le
2\exp\left(-\frac{nt^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]

Taking a union bound over \(p^2\) pairs \((j,k)\),

\[
\mathbb P\left(\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\ge t\right)
\le
2p^2\exp\left(-\frac{nt^2}{2B_0^4}\right).
\]

Let \(t=B_1\lambda_0\), where \(\lambda_0=\sqrt{\log(p/\delta)/n}\). Choose for example

\[
B_1=2B_0^2.
\]

Then

\[
\frac{nB_1^2\lambda_0^2}{2B_0^4}
=
2\log(p/\delta),
\]

so

\[
\mathbb P\left(\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\ge B_1\lambda_0\right)
\le
2p^2 e^{-2\log(p/\delta)}
=
2\delta^2.
\]

For \(\delta\le 1\), this is at most \(2\delta\). Thus with \(k_1=2\),

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_1)\ge 1-k_1\delta,
\qquad
\Omega_1:=\left\{\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\le B_1\lambda_0\right\}.
}
\]

---

## (iii)

Fix \(\xi_0>1\). Assume \(\eta_0\) is sufficiently small, specifically

\[
B_1(1+\xi_0)^2\eta_0\le \frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{2}.
\]

Then set

\[
\nu_0^2:=\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{2}.
\]

Let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\) satisfy the cone condition

\[
\sum_{j\notin S}|b_j|
\le
\xi_0\sum_{j\in S}|b_j|.
\]

Write \(\|b_S\|_1=\sum_{j\in S}|b_j|\). On \(\Omega_1\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
b^T\tilde\Sigma b
&=b^T\Sigma b+b^T(\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma)b\\
&\ge b^T\Sigma b-\|\tilde\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\max}\|b\|_1^2\\
&\ge b^T\Sigma b-B_1\lambda_0\|b\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

By the cone condition,

\[
\|b\|_1
=
\|b_S\|_1+\|b_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|b_S\|_1.
\]

By (A3),

\[
b^T\Sigma b\ge (\nu_0^*)^2\|b\|_2^2
\ge
(\nu_0^*)^2\|b_S\|_2^2
\ge
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
b^T\tilde\Sigma b
&\ge
\frac{(\nu_0^*)^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2
-
B_1\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2\|b_S\|_1^2\\
&=
\frac{1}{s}
\left[
(\nu_0^*)^2
-
B_1s\lambda_0(1+\xi_0)^2
\right]
\|b_S\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using (A4), \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), hence

\[
b^T\tilde\Sigma b
\ge
\frac{1}{s}
\left[
(\nu_0^*)^2
-
B_1(1+\xi_0)^2\eta_0
\right]\|b_S\|_1^2
\ge
\frac{\nu_0^2}{s}\|b_S\|_1^2.
\]

Thus

\[
\boxed{
\nu_0^2\left(\sum_{j\in S}|b_j|\right)^2
\le
s\, b^T\tilde\Sigma b.
}
\]

This is the desired compatibility/restricted-eigenvalue condition for \(\tilde\Sigma\).

---

## (iv)

Define the empirical score vector

\[
G_n:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i
=
\frac1n X^T\varepsilon.
\]

Let \(c>0\) be the universal constant in the standard concentration inequality for sums of independent sub-Gaussian random variables. Conditional on the design \(x_1,\dots,x_n\), for each coordinate \(j\),

\[
(G_n)_j=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_{ij}\varepsilon_i.
\]

Since \(|x_{ij}|\le B_0\), the conditional sub-Gaussian variance proxy is bounded by \(C\sigma^2 B_0^2/n\). Therefore there exists a constant \(B_2=B_2(\sigma,B_0)\) such that

\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|(G_n)_j\right|\ge B_2\lambda_0\mid x_1,\dots,x_n\right)
\le
2\exp\{-2\log(p/\delta)\}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\mathbb P\left(\left|(G_n)_j\right|\ge B_2\lambda_0\right)
\le
2\left(\frac{\delta}{p}\right)^2.
\]

By the union bound over \(j=1,\dots,p\),

\[
\mathbb P\left(\|G_n\|_\infty\ge B_2\lambda_0\right)
\le
2p\left(\frac{\delta}{p}\right)^2
=
\frac{2\delta^2}{p}
\le
2\delta.
\]

Define

\[
\boxed{
\Omega_2:=
\left\{
\left\|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\varepsilon_i
\right\|_\infty
\le
B_2\lambda_0
\right\}.
}
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb P(\Omega_2)\ge 1-k_2\delta
}
\]

with \(k_2=2\).

Now choose

\[
\boxed{
\lambda
=
\frac{\xi_0+1}{\xi_0-1}\,B_2\lambda_0.
}
\]

On \(\Omega_2\),

\[
\|G_n\|_\infty\le B_2\lambda_0
=
\frac{\xi_0-1}{\xi_0+1}\lambda.
\]

Using the standard Lasso basic inequality and the compatibility condition from part (iii), one obtains on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\)

\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \left(x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\right)^2
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
}
\]

Here \(M_0\) depends only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\), not on \(n,p,s\).

For completeness, the basic argument is as follows. Let \(Q:=\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta=n^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^T\Delta)^2\). The Lasso basic inequality gives

\[
\frac12 Q
\le
G_n^T\Delta+\lambda(\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+\Delta\|_1).
\]

On \(\Omega_2\),

\[
G_n^T\Delta\le \|G_n\|_\infty\|\Delta\|_1.
\]

Also,

\[
\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+\Delta\|_1
\le
\|\Delta_S\|_1-\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac12Q+(\lambda-\|G_n\|_\infty)\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(\lambda+\|G_n\|_\infty)\|\Delta_S\|_1.
\]

Because of the choice of \(\lambda\), this implies

\[
\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|\Delta_S\|_1.
\]

Hence the compatibility condition applies:

\[
\nu_0^2\|\Delta_S\|_1^2\le sQ.
\]

Combining,

\[
Q
\le
\frac{4s(\lambda+\|G_n\|_\infty)^2}{\nu_0^2}
\lesssim s\lambda_0^2,
\]

and similarly,

\[
\|\Delta\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|\Delta_S\|_1
\lesssim s\lambda_0.
\]

---

## (v)

By part (i),

\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta.
\]

On \(\Omega_1\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
&=
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta+\Delta^T(\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma)\Delta\\
&\le
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
+
\|\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|\Delta\|_1^2\\
&\le
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
+
B_1\lambda_0\|\Delta\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), part (iv) gives

\[
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^T\Delta)^2
\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2,
\]

and

\[
\|\Delta\|_1\le M_0s\lambda_0.
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using (A4), \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), so

\[
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]

Define

\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]

Thus on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,

\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta.
\]

with \(k_2=2\).

Now choose

\[
\boxed{
\lambda
=
\frac{\xi_0+1}{\xi_0-1}\,B_2\lambda_0.
}
\]

On \(\Omega_2\),

\[
\|G_n\|_\infty\le B_2\lambda_0
=
\frac{\xi_0-1}{\xi_0+1}\lambda.
\]

Using the standard Lasso basic inequality and the compatibility condition from part (iii), one obtains on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\)

\[
\boxed{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \left(x_i^T(\hat\beta-\beta^*)\right)^2
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0^2,
}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
\le
M_0 s\lambda_0.
}
\]

Here \(M_0\) depends only on \(B_0,\sigma,\xi_0,\nu_0\), not on \(n,p,s\).

For completeness, the basic argument is as follows. Let \(Q:=\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta=n^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^T\Delta)^2\). The Lasso basic inequality gives

\[
\frac12 Q
\le
G_n^T\Delta+\lambda(\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+\Delta\|_1).
\]

On \(\Omega_2\),

\[
G_n^T\Delta\le \|G_n\|_\infty\|\Delta\|_1.
\]

Also,

\[
\|\beta^*\|_1-\|\beta^*+\Delta\|_1
\le
\|\Delta_S\|_1-\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac12Q+(\lambda-\|G_n\|_\infty)\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1
\le
(\lambda+\|G_n\|_\infty)\|\Delta_S\|_1.
\]

Because of the choice of \(\lambda\), this implies

\[
\|\Delta_{S^c}\|_1\le \xi_0\|\Delta_S\|_1.
\]

Hence the compatibility condition applies:

\[
\nu_0^2\|\Delta_S\|_1^2\le sQ.
\]

Combining,

\[
Q
\le
\frac{4s(\lambda+\|G_n\|_\infty)^2}{\nu_0^2}
\lesssim s\lambda_0^2,
\]

and similarly,

\[
\|\Delta\|_1
\le
(1+\xi_0)\|\Delta_S\|_1
\lesssim s\lambda_0.
\]

---

## (v)

By part (i),

\[
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
=
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta.
\]

On \(\Omega_1\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
&=
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta+\Delta^T(\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma)\Delta\\
&\le
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
+
\|\Sigma-\tilde\Sigma\|_{\max}\|\Delta\|_1^2\\
&\le
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
+
B_1\lambda_0\|\Delta\|_1^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

On \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\), part (iv) gives

\[
\Delta^T\tilde\Sigma\Delta
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i^T\Delta)^2
\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2,
\]

and

\[
\|\Delta\|_1\le M_0s\lambda_0.
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
&\le
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1\lambda_0(M_0s\lambda_0)^2\\
&=
M_0s\lambda_0^2
+
B_1M_0^2s^2\lambda_0^3\\
&=
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2s\lambda_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using (A4), \(s\lambda_0\le \eta_0\), so

\[
\Delta^T\Sigma\Delta
\le
\left(M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0\right)s\lambda_0^2.
\]

Define

\[
M_1:=M_0+B_1M_0^2\eta_0.
\]

Thus on \(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2\),

\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\hat\beta)^2\}
\le
\mathbb E_{\rm out}\{(y_0-x_0^T\beta^*)^2\}
+
M_1 |S_{\beta^*}|\lambda_0^2.
}
\]

Moreover,

\[
\mathbb P(\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2)
\ge
1-(k_1+k_2)\delta.
\]
